exposure: route-specific complications of birth (vaginal vs. cesarean)
chronic and pregnancy-related comorbidities (hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, anemia, gestational diabetes, depression, anxiety)
outcome: incidence of chronic and pregnancy-related comorbidities
cohort: The cohort consisted of 988,480 birth admissions from 159 Illinois hospitals between January 2016 and June 2023.
finding: From 2016 to 2023, the rates of Severe Maternal Morbidity (SMM) and birth complications in Illinois increased, correlating with a rise in the reporting of chronic, prepregnancy, and pregnancy-related comorbidities.
mod_finding: Cesarean births were associated with a significantly higher rate of Severe Maternal Morbidity (3.2%) compared to vaginal births (0.9%), and cesarean birth complications increased by 48.9% over the study period.
